transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Wednesday, October 21. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Tiger Shroff shooting case: Police lens on Lawrence's US-based aide Randeep Malik. Anil Pandit Pandit and Shroff 's shooter Rehan both reported to Malik and were considered "his men" till a few months ago, a source said. Rehan had been earlier tasked by Malik and Pandit with a shooting incident in Sonipat as well. "Rehan was shown the same 'American dream' that Malik had shown Pandit in the past," a source said. Musk ordered Starlink slowdown, kept Ukraine and Trump administration in dark. US officials, however, have denied ordering any slowdown. Defence secretary Pete Hegseth said Washington had not directed any reduction in the satellite services, while secretary of state Marco Rubio maintained that the White House was not responsible for the reported disruption. Speaking to reporters, Hegseth said the US military had not instructed any changes to the satellite service used by Ukraine. Identify, defeat forces against India: Modi calls for unity, self-reliance. PM urges parties, institutions to put nation first; says national self-respect and strength key to overcoming challenges Dale Steyn's 18-year-old record falls as Harmer scripts history against Australia. Simon Harmer made headlines with an impressive 82 in the second Test against Australia, eclipsing the previous record of 76 runs held by Dale Steyn for South African No. 9 batsmen. His performance was vital in rescuing South Africa from a challenging position of 110-6. Partnering with Temba Bavuma, their formidable eighth-wicket alliance totaled 183 runs. In talks with Reliance to refine more Venezuelan oil: Marco Rubio. US secretary of state Marco Rubio is visiting Jamnagar Wednesday to tour the Reliance refinery and, in a lastminute change of schedule, is likely to spend the night there. He was earlier scheduled to leave around 9pm and return to Mumbai. In Jamnagar, he will have dinner with Mukesh Ambani at the Vantara centre. Rubio's visit to Jamnagar comes within weeks of a vicious attack on Ambani by Elon Musk. Florida couple missed 66 mortgage payments; man's bank lawsuit rejected. A Florida couple missed 66 monthly mortgage payments on their Naples property, triggering a foreclosure dispute that began in 2009. During the legal battle, Gregory Brian Myers agreed to deposit $5,000 monthly while appealing the foreclosure. He later sued U.S. Bank, alleging it had violated their agreement. 'Russia a big machine': Trump says Ukraine 'has to want' to settle war with Putin. US president Trump pointed to Russia's ability to sustain its military campaign and capture territory, portraying Moscow as having the upper hand in the conflict. "Russia is a big machine - they just keep grinding forward, and that's what they've done. They've taken a very large piece of land," he said. 'Darlings' actor Divya Vinekar passes away. Divya Vinekar's sudden departure was revealed by RJ Rohini Ramnathan via social media, marking an emotional moment for many. Requesting privacy for the grieving family, Ramnathan provided details for the cremation for those eager to honor Vinekar's memory. She graced screens with memorable performances in 'Darlings' and 'Jalsa', known for her professionalism and kindness, and her legacy continues to resonate within the film community. 5-year-old with neurological condition walks 30 laps for 30 days, raises $100K. Gregor Corse, a five-year-old boy from Scotland with an undiagnosed neurological condition, has raised over $100,000 for Inclusive Orkney by walking 30 laps around his house daily for 30 days. His inspiring determination earned him the Youngest Fundraiser of the Year title at the 2026 Pride of Britain Awards. He now hopes to raise more money. Florida homeowners denied legal fees after $157K Ian repair dispute. In a recent decision, a Florida appeals court determined that homeowners Susan Reed and Kent Lonngren are ineligible to collect legal fees from Citizens Property Insurance. The couple had contested repairs linked to Hurricane Ian's 2022 storm damage. The court concluded that Citizens had fulfilled its duties, even while the homeowners pursued legal action during the appraisal phase, indicating that Citizens acted in good faith throughout the claim.

transcript.text: Next, science and technology. Indian IT firms eye $20m–$60m US and European AI targets in outbound M and A push. YouTube might be testing hiding the dislike button. YouTube appears to be testing hiding the dislike button on videos, as reported by 9to5Google. At least two users on X have recently shared screenshots of the dislike button now being placed in the three-dots submenu, and a user on Reddit also shared an image of the dislike button being absent for them. Right now, Anthropic pitches AI safety bill that may block a model if 50+ people could be killed. The proposed policy seems to offer protections against AI run amok but actually forbids federal agencies from blocking a model's release without the permission of a judge. Scientists finally uncover why statins can cause muscle pain. Scientists have uncovered a surprising reason why statins, the widely prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs that help prevent heart attacks and strokes, can sometimes cause muscle pain, weakness, and even severe muscle damage. Using advanced imaging technology, researchers discovered that statins can attach to a crucial protein in muscle cells and force open a channel that normally controls calcium flow. This causes calcium to leak continuously, potentially damaging muscle tissue. Judge dismisses Sam Altman's sister's sexual abuse lawsuit. On Tuesday, US District Judge Zachary Bluestone dismissed the lawsuit Ann Altman filed last year alleging that her brother, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, had sexually abused her throughout her childhood. As reported earlier by The Guardian, the judge wrote that over the past year, Ann had failed to appear for an independent medical examination or SpaceX and Tesla boards form special committees to review merger. Elon Musk likes the idea but says he is not on either committee, which is made up of independent directors. Hurricane warning maps are improving, but a dangerous problem remains. A new study reveals that improved hurricane forecast graphics may help people identify threatened areas without making them more likely to recognize the danger or take protective action. Researchers also found that a widespread misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists, highlighting a potentially dangerous gap between accurate forecasts and public preparedness. Britain seeks to break Apples grip on contactless payments. APPLE-BRITAIN-REGULATION:Britain seeks to break Apple's grip on contactless payments Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program. Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday that the Trump administration was giving right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million bounty program for members of the public to report fraud. In December 2025, Shirley published a viral video alleging fraud at daycares in Minnesota that were operated by members Hugging Face CEO warns that Netflix's OpenAI hack documentary isn't accurate. Before you share the Netflix documentary "AI Gone Rogue" take note. Clem Delangue, Hugging Face's co-founder who is featured in the film, says it went "full doomer mode" and isn't accurate. Astronomers uncover new secrets of the Universe's first five minutes. Scientists have achieved a major breakthrough in understanding the Universe's earliest moments, measuring the amount of helium formed in the first five minutes after the Big Bang with unprecedented precision. Using one of the world's most powerful telescopes, an international team studied 15 remarkably pristine galaxies that act as cosmic time capsules, preserving clues from nearly 13.8 billion years ago. Enterprise software costs threaten AI investment, innovation as firms spend 28 percent of budgets on unwanted changes: Report. Large enterprises may face growing constraints on innovation and artificial intelligence (AI) investments as vendor-driven software upgrades, migrations and licensing changes consume an average of 28 per cent of their software budgets, according to a report by Origina published in collaboration with Thinkers50. Google's more personalized Gemini AI is heading to your car. Google is bringing Personal Intelligence to Gemini AI in your car. With this update, Gemini in Android Auto and cars with Google built-in can tap into your information across Google apps, including Gmail, Calendar, Maps, Photos, YouTube, and Search. As an example, Google says you can ask Gemini about your flight status if you're driving Anthropic's cloud partnerships are getting messy. Anthropic is reportedly struggling to secure enough compute from cloud providers that increasingly view it as a competitor, even as its infrastructure spending balloons ahead of a planned November IPO. Scientists discover a surprising link between vitamin C and cancer survival. A surprising clinical trial suggests that taking vitamin C daily could improve survival in people with precancerous blood disorders and early-stage blood cancers. Patients receiving the supplement had fewer adverse events and showed a promising survival advantage, raising hopes that a common vitamin could help protect against leukemia-related complications. Deepinder Goyal's Temple wearable pre-orders open November 1: How to order, expected price, colours and features. Deepinder Goyal's Temple wearable will open pre-orders on November 1, 2026, with six colour options planned for the launch edition. The device uses optical sensors to track cerebral blood flow and generates an Entropy score to indicate physiological strain. Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says. Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday. Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also SpaceX's AI business is beating expectations. SpaceX hit profitably in the third-quarter, with net income of $4.4 billion. AI was the engine. Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic "squid" unlike anything ever seen. Scientists have identified the "fattest" belemnite ever discovered, a bizarre, barrel-shaped squid relative that lived in Wyoming's ancient seas 160 million years ago. The exceptionally rare fossils reveal a creature unlike anything previously known, potentially a predator of smaller squid-like animals and a surprising survivor of a supposedly vanished family. Apple's 'Pro and tell' event on October 28: Touchscreen MacBook Pro, M6 Macs, iPad mini. Apple has announced a product launch event in Los Angeles, teasing new devices under the tagline 'Pro and tell'. The company is expected to unveil a touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro, an M6-powered iMac and the iPad mini 8 with an OLED display.

transcript.title: Development and policy
transcript.text: Now to development, infrastructure and government policy. India's $7 billion electric bus plan and more city news. A New Paradigm for Africa's Wealth: The India-Japan Trilateral Promise. India's economy growing despite West Asia conflict, Rajnath Singh says in Tajikistan. Rubio visits India seeking relief from global energy crunch. India, US share extraordinary alignment on issues that matter: Rubio. India's EV transition hinges on infrastructure, financing and policy support. Stellantis India Aims to Cut Vehicle Development Time to 24 Months. US targets $500 bn bilateral trade with India in three years, says Ambassador Sergio Gor. India PE-VC Investments Shift Towards Infrastructure and Hard Assets.

transcript.title: Across India
transcript.text: Turning to the big national stories. Delhi high court cites national security, junks CIC order to IAF on PMs' foreign trips. Allowing a petition by the Central Public Information Officer of Directorate of Personal Services, Air Headquarters, Justice Amit Mahajan held the IAF was justified in denying access to the records under section 8 of RTI that exempts disclosure of information that could jeopardise national security or pose a risk to a person's life and physical safety. India and United States to boost defence, energy ties, Marco Rubio says trade deal close. Rubio's second visit to India comes against the backdrop of the US's Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which is intended to penalise countries purchasing Russian oil, and Trump's subsequent temporary suspension of related tariffs. India maintains that its oil procurement is essential not only for its own energy security but also for the stability of global markets. Rubio lauded the "substantial progress" made by India in diversifying its energy portfolio. Police lens on Lawrence Bishnoi's aide Randeep Malik in Tiger Shroff shooting case. Anil Pandit Pandit and Shroff 's shooter Rehan both reported to Malik and were considered "his men" till a few months ago, a source said. Rehan had been earlier tasked by Malik and Pandit with a shooting incident in Sonipat as well. "Rehan was shown the same 'American dream' that Malik had shown Pandit in the past," a source said. India, US 'perfectly aligned' on key issues: Marco Rubio; defends ties with Pakistan. Addressing a gathering of India Inc's leading business figures, Rubio said the relationship between the two countries could help shape the future of the global economy, particularly as advances in artificial intelligence and quantum computing transform industries and societies. "I truly believe the relationship between US and India is defining, in many ways, in a positive way, what the 21st century can look like," he said. In talks with Reliance to refine more Venezuelan oil: US secretary of state Marco Rubio. US secretary of state Marco Rubio is visiting Jamnagar Wednesday to tour the Reliance refinery and, in a lastminute change of schedule, is likely to spend the night there. He was earlier scheduled to leave around 9pm and return to Mumbai. In Jamnagar, he will have dinner with Mukesh Ambani at the Vantara centre. Rubio's visit to Jamnagar comes within weeks of a vicious attack on Ambani by Elon Musk. AAIB chief gets a year's extension as many key probes, including AI 171, on. People in the know say while the aviation ministry "keeps the aircraft accident investigating agency at an arm's length and does not interfere in its working in any way," it is taking steps to strengthen the AAIB. The bureau's lab has been recently upgraded and it now has the capability to download cockpit voice recorder and digital flight data recorder (black box) to know the conversation in the flight deck and the flight parameters till before an event being investigated. Two Andaman, one Chhattisgarh site added to Unesco World Heritage tentative list. India has added three sites to its tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage status, including the Karst-mud-volcano Complex. The sites are located in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Chhattisgarh, and the Archaeological Survey of India played a crucial role. Inclusion on this list is necessary for future nominations to the UNESCO World Heritage List. Currently, India possesses 45 UNESCO World Heritage Sites, ranking sixth in the world. Delhi BJP leader burns giant cockroach effigy; CJP founder responds with SRK's 'Swades' song. During Dussehra celebrations in Delhi, a 30-foot cockroach effigy was burned alongside traditional effigies of Ravan. Organizers stated that the effigy symbolized filth and promoted cleanliness in line with health awareness initiatives. Leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party reacted sharply, suggesting the move provided them with free publicity. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra remarked that cockroaches symbolize chaos and filth, reflecting public sentiment. 'Youth on streets are revolutionaries': Uddhav Thackeray calls for 'regime change'. During the vibrant Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, Uddhav Thackeray rallied his supporters, highlighting the significance of youth activism in addressing the alleged electoral irregularities impacting the fresh electorate. He proclaimed that the saffron identity is a legacy of his party, urging a reformation in the political climate and the prominent display of the saffron flag, echoing the influence of Bal Thackeray in his passionate address. PM Modi invokes 'Ram Rajya', warns against people hurting India's image - top quotes from Dussehra event. Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the Dussehra celebrations and highlighted the importance of public welfare. He emphasized the need for social justice and self-reliance as central to national development. Modi reminded attendees of the ideals of Lord Ram, focusing on justice and equal opportunities. He encouraged recognizing India's potential while serving the poor and marginalized. Air India Express flight suffers bird strike, lands safely in Bengaluru. An Air India Express flight en route from Bhogapuram to Bengaluru encountered a bird strike on Monday, yet all 148 passengers and crew emerged safely. Following the event, technical teams diligently inspected the aircraft, confirming it was in good condition for future flights. Notably, a comparable bird strike event affected an Emirates flight just days earlier on October 17. No double standards on terror, need unified action to dismantle its entire ecosystem: Rajnath at SCO. Defence minister Rajnath Singh, in the presence of Pakistan's deputy PM and foreign minister Mohammad Ishaq Dar at a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting in Dushanbe, said on Tuesday that there should not be "double standards" on terrorism as it "not only harms innocent lives but also investment and commerce". Amit Shah meets families of anti-drug campaigners killed in Punjab; targets AAP on open drug trade. Amit Shah visited families of drug-related victims in Punjab, expressing condolences and discussing safety issues. He criticised the AAP government for its failure to tackle the drug menace effectively. Shah highlighted the dangers faced by those who oppose drug trafficking in the state. The recent murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota escalated political tensions in Punjab. 'Expect partners to show zero tolerance on terrorism': EAM thanks US for handing over Tahawwur Rana. External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday hailed ties between India and the US, saying the partnership between the two countries had grown over the past few decades despite their share of differences. 'Felt very happy': Annamalai welcomes Bhagwat's remarks on Muslims' place in India. K Annamalai lauded Mohan Bhagwat's recent statements on the significance of religious inclusivity in India. Speaking at a Faith Leaders Conference in New York, Bhagwat encouraged the embrace of diverse communities, including Muslims, reiterating the value of dignity for all. Annamalai pointed out the rising global fascination with Indian civilization, stressing the necessity for leaders and citizens to embody the nation's established ideals.

transcript.title: Around the world
transcript.text: And finally, here is what is happening around the world. Man charged with attack on Australia MP to face court. Brendan Nugent's family say they have known Helen Haines, who remains in a critical condition, for more than 20 years. Alberta's decisive decision to stay in Canada gives Carney backing to take on Trump. The overwhelming vote by Alberta to stay in Canada gives Mark Carney political capital to focus on remaking the country's economy, writes the BBC's Lyse Doucet. Sudan army drones hit mourners and fuel market killing more than 300 people, sources say. A truck carrying people to a funeral and a market alleged to be supplying fuel to the RSF were targeted. Swimmer, 65, killed in shark attack off South Africa's east coast. Janine Lochrenberg, 65, was out on her daily morning swim with her club when she was attacked, her family tell the BBC. North Korea publishes photos of Kim Jong Un - why do rumours of his death keep coming back?. North Korean state media has published photos of the dictator with his daughter after the unsubstantiated rumour spread. Tourist found guilty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure. The man testified that he snatched Peachy from its enclosure at the Flamingo hotel and casino after drinking 30 to 40 beers, but did not mean any harm. Suspect arrested after historic town hall set alight - French media. The spire of the clock tower at Limoges city hall dramatically collapsed as it was engulfed in flames on Saturday. Kenya cult leader's children still being starved weeks before trial, son says. Dan Mackenzie initially defended his father but now says he felt he had to report his own grandmother. Cornell Jane Doe says embattled university head doubted her gang-rape allegation. As a no-confidence vote looms, Cornell says the characterisation of the head's reaction is "incorrect". Seventh day of violent clashes between Albanian protesters and police. Almost 300 people have been injured, more than half of them police, as violent anti-government demonstrations show no sign of easing.

transcript.title: Sign-off
transcript.text: That is your briefing. Stay sharp, and have a strong day.
